scope: all 133 stored OOF vectors in artifacts/predictions vs the certified champion
method: recomputed pooled OOF AUC for every *_oof.npy, per-fold paired deltas vs v7 on the immutable primary folds, logit correlation, best single-weight logit blend over w in {0.02,0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20,0.30,0.40,0.50}
finding: No stored vector has a positive mean paired fold delta against v7. Even with hindsight selection over 133 vectors x 7 weights (~930 comparisons) the largest achievable blend delta is +1.54e-5, which is at the noise level of that search. The (AUC, rho) frontier is flat on its useful side: at a correlation floor of 0.998 the best measured delta falls to +4.33e-6.

scope: the two certified v7 parents: route (pooled 0.9615159787) and aux10 (0.9614187093); 5 primary folds; 7 composition rules vs the deployed 50/50 logit mean
method: C1 nested per-fold weight on a 17-point grid fitted on FIT rows; C2 within-block rank average; C3 FIT-row empirical-CDF quantile average; C4 5-feature L2 logistic on FIT rows; C5 two Platt scalings on FIT rows then averaged; C6 arithmetic probability mean; C7 geometric probability mean. Promotion: mean paired fold delta >= 1.5e-5, t >= 2.5, 5/5 folds positive, Holm <= 0.05
finding: The deployed 50/50 logit mean is the optimum of the entire low-variance composition family. Every zero-parameter nonlinearity (rank, CDF, probability mean, geometric mean) is strictly worse by 6e-6 to 1.1e-5; the FIT-fitted rules recover at most +1.7e-6. The 0.0056 aggregation-loss AUC mass reported by the phase-19 atlas is therefore not recoverable by any reparameterisation of the two parent scores.

scope: the 10 certified aux10 members and the TabPFN route seed pair (1201, 1202) on primary fold 0
method: recompute each member's pooled OOF AUC and every leave-one-out mean; recompute the seed-1201 vs seed-1202 route AUC and their logit average on fold 0; quote the measured internal2->internal4 portfolio conversion from the phase-18 audit
finding: The aux10 equal mean is optimal to within 2.4e-6. Seed averaging the route is real at the parent level (+8.93e-5 on fold 0) but converts to only ~7% at the portfolio level because route and aux10 have logit correlation 0.9977; the independently measured internal2->internal4 arm confirms the conversion (route +5.34e-5 -> portfolio +3.818e-6). Any parent-local improvement therefore needs ~+2e-4 at the parent to reach the +1.5e-5 portfolio gate.

prereg: configs/phase24/segment_gate_prereg.json sha256 f2ab010904607a2aff01addb34e9f62a5f9b5ad46dffca14a745307918974835 (v1.1: two empty family prefixes replaced by conf/resid before any statistic was computed)
scope: 8 deterministic family representatives x 2 label-free segment definitions = 16 frozen tests; single gate weight per fold fitted on FIT rows inside the segment
method: S1 = 16-column rating key frequency 1 (304,464 rows); S2 = frequency <= 3 (431,005 rows); weight grid 0..0.5 step 0.05 maximising AUC on FIT rows inside the segment; rows outside the segment keep the champion logit
finding: The FIT-optimal gate weight inside the segment is exactly zero in 11 of 16 tests, i.e. every candidate family actively hurts inside the slice on FIT rows. The best measured delta is +2.8e-6 (t 0.85). The champion's deficit on sparse-key rows is not a composition problem and is not repaired by smoother families.

scope: exact feature-vector overlap train<->test, within train, within test; 16-column rating-key concentration
method: pandas hash_pandas_object over the 21 predictor columns (and separately over the 16 rating/categorical columns)
finding: There is no exact duplicate leak across train and test and none within either split. The only dense key structure is the 16-column rating key, whose median group size is 1 and whose p90 is 3; 17.9% of rows sit in keys with >=20 members. That structure is already carried by the fold-safe target-encoding blocks and by the original-data target statistics in the rich view.

scope: source-distribution CV anchor at 130k and 65k rows; matched leave-one-out profile determinism on the 16-column rating/categorical key in both populations; delay contribution and delay-block label rates
method: LightGBM num_leaves=255, lr 0.03, extra_trees, 4000 rounds, inner 10% early stopping; StratifiedKFold(5, seed 20261010) on the source; groupby-transform leave-one-out group means on the 16-column key; zero-duplicate check on the source feature matrix
finding: The source population is nearly deterministic at a fixed discrete profile (LOO AUC 0.9710) while the synthetic population is not (0.9253), despite repeating MORE profiles (mean group 1.81 vs 1.25). The generator smoothed the label function. Two alternative explanations are refuted by measurement: delays carry only 3.28e-4 of the source model (0.988806 -> 0.988478), and the source has zero duplicate feature vectors, so neither the delay rewrite nor duplicate leakage explains the 0.027 gap. This is the mechanism behind the shared-error mass and the 0.9618-0.9620 plateau.

scope: all 17 submitted candidates, remote submission list joined to the local manifest on the CSV stem
method: public score minus pooled OOF per submission; common offset removed; residual spread; OOF-on-public regression; private-size scaling of the paired spread by sqrt(rows_public/rows_private); three transfer models for P(v6>v7)
finding: After removing the common -3.69e-4 public-split offset, the OOF slope on public is 0.724 with r 0.819: OOF explains about two thirds of the public-score variance across submissions. The per-submission residual spread (1.21e-4, 1.72e-4 paired) equals the whole band separating the public top (0.96159) from v7 (0.96146). v6 carries a +6.73e-5 public-transfer advantage over v7 and the second-best residual in the cohort, so P(v6>v7) on private is 15.4% (noise-only), 26.6% (half-shrunk) or 40.8% (real). This quantifies the value of the free second final slot and the futility of chasing OOF gains below ~2e-4. It postdates the phase-close commit and refines the finalist decision only; it does not reopen modelling.

prereg: configs/phase24/candidate_x_prereg.json (frozen before the public measurement, which was never spent)
scope: 27 downloadable external OOF vectors (11 Deotte TFM, 8 goodpjw2008 TabPFN/TabICL, 7 najiama blends) measured on our immutable primary and shadow folds
method: pooled AUC and per-fold paired deltas vs certified v7 on primary (seed 20261010) and shadow (seed 777001); nested logistic stacks with weights fitted on FIT rows only; fixed-weight blend 0.15 v7 + 0.85 nj05
finding: Our own model store caps at 0.96185; the honest public frontier is ~0.9622. Deotte's 11 TFMs are individually and jointly worse than v7 (best 0.961145; nested stack 0.961236), so the gain is not a better TFM but a specific diverse blend: nj05 reaches 0.962234 (+3.75e-4, t 11.4, 5/5) and a fixed 0.85/0.15 blend with v7 reaches 0.962247 (+3.89e-4, t 13.4, 5/5 on primary and shadow). The public top (0.96341 on 10-20, 0.96370 reported 10-23) is public-surface selection, not model quality: 128-133 submissions for the leaders, and the public notebooks state that part of the gain is public noise with no independent CV claim.
